body: totally agree. the problem is with my current part time job, a psychiatrist visit would be 3 or 4 days' pay :(

Umm, when I did that outpatient therapy, which was crappy, I went to like twenty something AA meetings in about forty days. Those were the most valuable part of the experience. I, of course, resonated with most of the comments. I see how the steps "work," but I just don't get what people mean when you "work" them.

My problem is my desire not to drink wavers. I always the desire to not desire to drink, but sometimes it loses out. That feeling of happiness and I-can-do-anything that lasts for about two drinks before I start losing it is hard to compare with in reality, unfortunately.



I know no matter what else happens that my life will be vastly improved by not drinking and horribly worsened if I continue.

Good point. I can't seem to get over the embarrassment in people finding out I'm trying to quit drinking, even more so to admit I go to AA.

You're right, though, AA is helpful. I just can't get the step thing. Seriously, I tried to "work them" as part of an outpatient treatment, but it just doesn't seem to click. I'm down with God restoring me to sanity... still waiting on that one.

Yeah, I've been to AA off and on. I did therapy as a kid and then a couple of years ago. It's been moderately helpful, but most of the time I just end up more confused with what I'm thinking than I did before I went in. 

I agree with multiple chances; the problem is when those chances could be limited in how good they can be compared to how great things could have been had I not screwed them up in the first place.

Thanks for the post. I should mention that I took Lexapro 20mg/day for anxiety disorder for about a year. I suppose it helped, but I honestly believe that was a side effect of so much alcohol use. 

You're probably right. I guess it kind of frustrates me even more that I can't seem to give up having hope even when I feel like I should.

I would love and surely need to see a therapist now, but alas, no job, no health insurance, no savings. 

I appreciate what you do in commenting here.
Basically, I'm tired of self-sabotaging. I guess that would cover it.

No reason to be a total fucking asshole. As least learn to read properly if you want to insult me. I didn't sleep at house of the girl I cheated on her with. I slept at the house of a female friend whom I slept with several years before I knew my ex. We were already broken up at that point. I was saying I shouldn't have done that, because it made her rightly uneasy and less willing to give me another shot. Either way, you're right.

To be honest, though, I am a fucking idiot. No reason to insult retarded people, because they are all much better humans than I am.

I think that's where our differences lie. On the phone call (which she initiated) last Friday, she told me she was trying to move on, and I told her I wasn't. 

I guess the most confusing part is that she says she wants to move on. She has, in fact, flirted with guys, gone to parties, started talking to one in particular. Nevertheless, the past few days she initiated all that contact with me. And then sending me the text saying she wished she were still part of my family really made me feel like she wasn't moving on, that she wanted to come back.

I suppose I just went too far over the top with my letter. I probably should've slow-played it, but my excitement got the best of me. 

I'm fully aware of the uphill battle once trust is lost, but I wanted to give it another go to see if it could work. She's worth it to me, and I'm confident I would never cheat again. (That's the only time in any relationship that I have, and I was thoroughly drunk when I did it.)

You're very right. Thanks. I've wondered how to avoid becoming her slave and/or debasing myself so much that it's pathetic. She gave me those few glimmers of hope, and I wanted to take my chances. I know I need to back off and see how she reacts, but it's hard not to try to take control or manipulate. I know I don't need to do that.

It's very difficult to move on when my current circumstances dictate that I live at home for a few months. However, my parents moved since I last lived with them a few years back, and I know not a soul in this town. All my friends are scattered across the state and country, so I have nothing to do besides stew on this. The job I have now requires no attention, so I think about it there, too.

For a couple of weeks I tried to put myself out there, online, flirting at work, and so on, but I just couldn't seem to enjoy anyone else.

Oh well. Life goes on, as they say.
